what: A one-day plan for this trip map, carried entirely in the URL query string. Nothing is stored on a server.

params.city: one of the leg ids: seoul | jeju | busan
params.stops: comma-separated place ids, in visiting order; duplicates collapse; at most 12
params.day: YYYY-MM-DD, and one of the trip's own dates. A label, and the only thing that decides which weekday closures apply; no schedule is computed from it. The plan pane offers the trip's fifteen days as chips, and a day with no date is a valid day.
params.title: percent-encoded free text, at most 60 characters

resolve.how: Each id in ?stops= is the `id` field of an entry in the PLACES array, published as JSON in the <script type="application/json" id="trip-data"> element in this file.
placeFields: closed (optional, weekday keys; [] means open every day)
resolve.categories: The `cats` object in that same #trip-data block maps `cat` to {label, emoji, color}.
resolve.hoursCaveat: Opening hours are a structured field, `hours`, in the 24h grammar `Daily 09:00-22:00` / `Mon-Fri 18:30-26:00; Sat,Sun 15:00-26:00` / `Daily 10:00-14:50,17:00-21:30` / `24h`, optionally with `; closed Tue` and `; LO 21:00`. A closing time past 24:00 is the next morning, so 26:00 is 02:00. `closed` is the weekday keys the place is shut, and an empty array means open every day. `ko` is the Korean name and `signature` is what to order. Prices still appear only as prose in `meta` or `note` - quote those, do not parse them. There are still no arrival times, dwell times or durations anywhere: `hours` says when a door is open, never when you will be standing at it.

notRepresented: arrival times, dwell times and durations of any kind
rail time between two stops - the routing table is rooted at the hotel only, so no station-to-station time exists anywhere in this file
how busy anywhere is, or how long the queue runs
directions: Each consecutive pair of stops gets a Naver Maps directions link built from the two lat/lng pairs. See naverDirUrl() in the inline script for the exact grammar.
goodUseOfThis: Read the plan, then add what the map cannot know: when each place is busy, what to order, how long a queue tends to run, and whether the order makes sense for the hours involved.
storedLocally: This browser also remembers the last day you were building, the category filters, night mode and which spots you have ticked off as visited. None of that is in the link and none of it is on a server: a link names stops, and a link that names stops always wins over what was remembered.
